title: Pretzel Day
logline: Michael replaces Stanley's annual Pretzel Day with Andy's welcome brunch, then tries to make it up to him with 212 pretzels, while Dwight tests Andy's sales claims and loses.
outline: A: Michael cancels Pretzel Day for Andy's brunch, then overcompensates with 212 pretzels for Stanley. B: Dwight tests Andy's sales claims; Andy outsells him and they agree to an armed truce. C: Stanley's one joy is rescued by Creed's cousin Gus and forty-one stale pretzels. Order: cold, A, B, C, A, B, C, A, B, A, tag.
theme: Being seen: the kind thing you do for someone can still be about you, and the small gift that's plainly meant can still matter.
storySoFar: Michael still chases Jan's approval; Jan keeps sending maybes and said in voicemail she isn't coming. Jim and Pam keep escalating Jell-O pranks on Dwight; Jim noticed Pam's earrings and Roy got it wrong. Pam is an artist and Jim is the first to really look at her sketches; her Dwight drawings hang on the crime wall. Roy keeps postponing the wedding. Angela thanks Dwight publicly for fax checks; Oscar and Kevin know and say nothing. Andy Bernard arrived from Stamford, held a Cornell mixer only Michael and Kevin attended, and is in an armed truce with Dwight. Michael keeps a folding chair for Toby. Gerald Boyd gave Scranton a barely pass. Stanley's countdown stands at 211 after Pretzel Day was moved to Andy's Welcome Brunch (Sunday). Creed has a cousin, Gus, with a pretzel van.

extras.name: Gus Hollander
extras.title: Owner, Hollander's Soft Pretzels
extras.voice: Gravelly, friendly, slightly nervous Ohio man who calls everyone 'chief'. Says the pretzels are fresh while holding a bag from last week. Not a good liar, not a bad man.

stateChanges.progress: Dwight's sales test lost to Andy (Andy 4 sales, Dwight 1). Truce re-armed: Dwight keeps the title of Michael's favorite, Andy keeps the crowd. They shook on it with a three-note fanfare.

Michael cancelled Pretzel Day for Andy's Sunday brunch, then bought 212 pretzels for Stanley. He wrote Stanley a note; Stanley said thank you. Michael's kindness was public and overwhelming, but it landed.

stateChanges.text: Stanley has 41 stale pretzels from Gus and a 212-pretzel stack from Michael in the break room. Andy's Welcome Brunch is Sunday with a banjo.
Michael's index card to Stanley: 'You are the one person here I never have to explain myself to.' Stanley keeps it.
Stanley's countdown: 212 at the cold open, 211 in the tag.
Michael's 'That's what she said' lands on silence again, this time to Stanley's countdown.
Kevin: 'Nobody say nothing.' Used in the cold open, the pretzel-van scene and the tag.
Andy's hold music is a banjo; Oscar: 'Actually, that's a banjo on hold.'

stateChanges.status: armed truce, mutual respect; Dwight keeps the title, Andy keeps the crowd

scenes.recap: Stanley accuses Kevin of eating his pretzels, and Kevin's one line is the only answer.

beats.text: Kevin. Did you eat the last pretzel out of my tin?
Nobody say nothing.

beats.caption: chews a pretzel with great concentration and no apology

beats.text: Kevin, you have salt on your face. Also on your tie.
Two hundred and twelve days. And Friday is Pretzel Day.

beats.caption: Across the bullpen, Dwight's lime Jell-O trophy wobbles on…

scenes.recap: Michael announces Pretzel Day has been replaced by Andy's Welcome Brunch, and the office reacts badly.

beats.text: Friends. Pretzel Day has... evolved.
Evolved into what?
The Andy Bernard Welcome Brunch. Sunday. With a banjo.
Pretzels are nice. But a brunch is a commitment to a community.
Question: who approved moving the Party Planning budget?
The Party Planning Committee was not consulted. Nobody consults the Party Planning Committee.
I approved it. Andy asked nicely. Nobody asks me nicely.
False. He asked with a banjo.
It's the one day I don't have to talk to anybody.
Stanley, you'll talk to Andy. Everybody talks to Andy.

lines: Pretzel Day is a great day. But Andy is a guest, and guests get the good stuff.
I'm a leader. Leaders make hard calls, like brunch. Stanley will understand. Eventually.

scenes.recap: Dwight demands proof of Andy's sales numbers and proposes a phone contest with Jim as witness.

beats.text: Question: how many sales did you close in Stamford last quarter?
Eleven! And one that was just a handshake. It counts.
False. A handshake is a courtesy.
Five accounts. Phone only. The loser surrenders the title of Michael's Second.
Big Tuna, you're the witness.
Why me?

lines: Andy is a fraud. I have been a fraud detector since birth.
I am the only person in this office who can count. Also, I can count to five.

scenes.recap: Creed offers Stanley a cousin with a pretzel van, and Stanley refuses to ask questions.

beats.text: My cousin Gus has a pretzel van. Gus owes me a van.
I'm not asking about Gus.
Nobody asked. That's why it's good stuff.
Gus is good man. Nobody say nothing.

beats.caption: Stanley fills in one crossword square, then another, very…

beats.text: Friday. Six a.m. Don't be late, Creed.

beats.caption: pours Stanley a coffee from a thermos labeled 'Ohio'

scenes.recap: Michael asks Toby whether he can expense 212 pretzels, and Toby reminds him what he moved.

beats.text: Toby, can a manager expense two hundred and twelve pretzels?
No.
Two hundred and twelve pretzels for one friend. That's a metaphor.
The pretzel budget went to Andy's brunch. You moved it.
I didn't move it. I redirected it toward warmth.

lines: Michael has never been kind to me. He set out a folding chair once. I sat in it. That was the high point.
He wants me to not tell HR. I'm HR. I'm going to think about it.

beats.text: Don't tell Jan about this. She'd find it sad. She finds everything sad except candles.

scenes.recap: Dwight and Andy race to call five accounts, and Andy's banjo hold music becomes the sound of the contest.

beats.caption: writes five account names on the whiteboard in block capitals

beats.text: Ten minutes. Begin.

beats.caption: dials Scranton Family Dental and asks about the receptionist's dog
reads the entire Dunder Mifflin catalog aloud to a voicemail
Ten minutes pass; the only sound is banjo hold music

beats.text: Actually, that's a banjo on hold.
Scranton Family Dental. Three cases. Dr. Patel says I'm 'a breath of fresh air.'
A tie is not a sales technique.
Dwight, my tie is my whole personality.
Four to one, Dwight. Good game.

scenes.recap: A van backs into the warehouse dock and Gus unloads forty-one pretzels for Stanley.

beats.text: Creed, why is a van backing into my dock?
It's a pretzel delivery. It isn't a van.
Gus Hollander, Hollander's Soft Pretzels. Forty-one pretzels, chief. Mustard in the bag.
Forty-one. I have two hundred and eleven days.
Pretzels aren't math, Stanley.
Gus has never been to prison. He's been close.
Don't ask him about the van.

beats.caption: takes a pretzel, bites, and does not smile, which is a smile for Stanley

lines: Forty-one pretzels is not a day. But it isn't nothing.
Don't put that on the wall.

beats.text: Thank you, Creed.

scenes.recap: Michael wheels in 212 pretzels for Stanley and gives a speech that makes everyone, including Stanley, want to leave.

beats.caption: wheels a rolling cart stacked with 212 pretzel boxes into the bullpen

beats.text: Michael, what is that?
Two hundred and twelve pretzels. One for each day Stanley has left. That's a lot of love.
That's a lot of pretzels, Michael.
It's not a lot. It's a number.
I have forty-one pretzels from Creed's cousin's van.
Stanley, you've been here two hundred and twelve days, and I want you to know you're not alone.
Please stop.
Pretzel good. Nobody say nothing.

lines: I'm not good at saying I care. I'm good at saying things at a volume.
Stanley doesn't know I'm his friend. Or he does, and he's mad about it.

scenes.recap: Dwight admits he closed one account, and he and Andy re-sign the truce with a three-note fanfare.

beats.text: Question: final results.
Four sales. A dental office, a hotel, and a guy who buys paper for his bird.

beats.caption: Dwight counts on his fingers, reaches one, and stops

beats.text: I still keep the title.
You keep the title. I keep the crowd.
Agreed. Armed truce.

beats.caption: sings a three-note fanfare while shaking Dwight's hand for one second too long

beats.text: Can I go now?

lines: Dwight is my rival. I respect that he's committed to being wrong about me.
His tie is wrong. But his heart is in a very specific place.

scenes.recap: Michael leaves a pretzel and a card on Stanley's desk, and Stanley reads it and finally says thank you.

beats.caption: leaves one pretzel and a folded index card on Stanley's desk

beats.text: Don't read that in front of me.

beats.caption: reads the index card twice, then a third time

beats.text: Michael.
Yes, I'm here. I'm always here. That's the problem.
Thank you.
That's what she said.

scenes.recap: The next morning Stanley counts down to 211, and Michael's callback lands on silence.

beats.text: Two hundred and eleven.
Two hundred and eleven. That's what she said.
Nobody say nothing.
Did I stutter?
